canonical_definition: Multimodal Reasoning is the ability to systematically draw logically coherent and contextually informed inferences by integrating visual and textual inputs, often involving perception-based analysis and spanning diverse tasks such as question answering, entity labeling, and cross-modal explanation. While most definitions emphasize combined vision-language processing for factual or contextual reasoning, some extend to include programmatic steps in chain-of-thought workflows, interdisciplinary applications, or integration of additional modalities like auditory cues. Disagreement exists in scope, with narrower operationalizations focusing on specific benchmarks (e.g., VQA) versus broader characterizations involving unified perception-reasoning architectures or multimodal document analysis.
